message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory rights designed to protect them from unfair treatment and to ensure safe, habitable living conditions. Below is a concise overview of key tenant rights under Texas law (Texas Property Code, Chapter 24) and related statutes: | Category | Key Rights | Practical Implications | |----------|------------|------------------------| | **Security Deposits** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit, two months for an unfurnished unit.
• Deposit must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear. | • Keep records of the unit’s condition at move‑in and move‑out. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, and pest control.
• Must keep the premises in a safe, sanitary condition. | • Report repairs promptly; if landlord fails, you may withhold rent or repair & deduct. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease; late fees are limited to 10% of the monthly rent. | • Pay on time to avoid penalties; if you’re late, communicate with the landlord. | | **Lease Terms** | • Written lease required for leases > 1 year.
• Lease must specify rent amount, due date, security deposit, and lease duration. | • Review lease carefully before signing; negotiate terms if needed. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter without notice (except emergencies). | • Landlords must give reasonable notice (usually 24 hours) before entering. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or handicap. | • If you suspect discrimination, file a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must provide written notice (30 days for nonpayment, 60 days for lease violations).
• Eviction requires a court order; landlords cannot forcibly remove tenants. | • Respond to notices promptly; seek legal advice if threatened with eviction. | | **Repair & Deduct** | • If landlord fails to repair, tenant may repair and deduct cost from rent, but only if the repair is necessary for habitability. | • Keep receipts and document the damage. | | **Right to Sublet** | • Tenants may sublet with landlord’s consent; landlords cannot unreasonably deny consent. | • Obtain written permission before subletting. | | **Notice of Lease Termination** | • Landlord must give 30 days’ notice to terminate a month‑to‑month lease. | • Provide 30 days’ notice if you plan to move out. | ### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** – Take photos, keep written communication, and keep copies of all lease documents. 2. **Know the Law** – Familiarize yourself with the Texas Property Code (Chapter 24) and local ordinances. 3. **Communicate Early** – Report maintenance issues promptly and keep a written record of your requests. 4. **Seek Legal Help** – If disputes arise, consult a tenant‑rights attorney or a local tenant‑advocacy organization. 5. **File Complaints** – For discrimination or unlawful eviction, file complaints with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the local housing authority. --- If you need a specific lease template or want to generate a contract that incorporates these rights, let me know the type of contract and parties involved, and I can help draft it.
